text:
maria: Heads-up — vendor quote just came back for H200 blocks. Lead times look long (14–20w) and price is up ~18% vs last year. Q4 ramp projection shows a +40% GPU-hour need vs our current commit. We should discuss commit window and whether we hedge with L40S or buy more H100 reservations.

jake: Can you drop the numbers? how many H200s are they offering, and what's the actual throughput delta vs L40S for our steady seq len=1024 workloads?

maria: Quote: 300 H200 GPUs (NVIDIA SXM) across us-west/us-east, 16GB interconnect nodes priced at $1.48/hour equivalent for reserved capacity. Lead time estimate 14–20w.

maria: Current forecast (Q4): baseline 850k GPU-hours, ramp scenarios up to 1.2M GPU-hours. We have ~600k committed today across Dedicated pools. So gap ~250–600k GPU-hours depending on scenario.

jake: For seq=1024 our perf tests show an H200 delivers ~1.9x tokens/sec vs L40S on the same model, and H200 latency tail is better under batching. L40S can help on cost but you'd need ~2x nodes to match throughput in many workloads.

sasha: Region availability note: vendor only guaranteed H200 shipments to us-west and eu-west in that window. APAC was explicitly excluded. If we rely on H200 for APAC SLAs, we'll need an alternate plan (L40S or H100 fallbacks) or cross-region routing.

lee: Cost sensitivity: at 1.2M GPU-hours, incremental cost for buying H200 reservations vs L40S mix is roughly +$420k over the quarter (fully amortized). Finance can stretch but prefer we show unit-cost delta and outage risk tradeoff.

maria: Proposal A: commit to 300 H200 (split 200 us-west, 100 eu-west) to cover peak inference baseline and autoscale. Proposal B: 150 H200 + 320 L40S in us-west + burst fallback to spot H100 for batch. Proposal C: no H200 commit; buy 800 L40S and optimize model quantization to reduce perf gap.

jake: Technical caveat for B: L40S NVMe behavior is fine for steady traffic but KV cache pressure grows; we'd need to tune KV eviction and raise batch window slightly. That will add ~6–12ms median latency in stress tests.

sasha: Also remember network egress at scale — L40S boxes push more outbound and we hit inter-rack bandwidth caps in our current pod configs. If we mix, need to re-evaluate top-of-rack links for the us-west cluster.

maria: @procurement-bot can you pull last year's lead time logs and actual ship dates for H200/H100/L40S so we have real delivery variance numbers?

procurement-bot: Pulling shipment history: H200 avg ship delta = 18w (sigma 3.2w), H100 avg = 10w (sigma 2.5w), L40S avg = 9w (sigma 2.1w). Also, 2025 Q4 had a 12% partial-fill rate for H200.

lee: Thanks. If H200 partial-fill risk is 12% we need contingency capacity plan. Finance prefers mixed hedge (some H200 + L40S) to reduce spend volatility.

maria: Actionable ask: we need a recommended commit shape and a procurement cutoff date to meet a minimum deployment by 2026-11-15. If vendor lead is 18w median, latest commit should be by 2026-07-21. Can eng provide a recommended mix by EOD tomorrow?

jake: I'll run a perf+cost sweep overnight comparing these three mixes (all H200 / mixed / all L40S) with our model profiles, including tail latency SLO hit and cost per 1k tokens. Will post results.

sasha: I'll map region availability constraints and validate network upgrade scope for the mixed option.

lee: I'll produce a quick P&L delta and risk buffer for each option.

maria: Quick note: if we push more to L40S, product wants a comms plan — user-facing latency might increase in some routes. Keep that flagged. :warning: 

jake: One more thing — H100 stocks at some distributors are low but still viable as a short-term fill for APAC if we decide to mix. Perf is between H200 and L40S for our workload.

maria: Perfect. Let's regroup tomorrow 10:30am PT. TL;DR: vendor quoted 300 H200 with long lead times; options are commit, hedge with L40S, or optimize and stick with current reserve; need eng/network/finance inputs by EOD tomorrow. :calendar:
